summary:
# NOTES: Frank Merriwell's Support; Or, A Triple Play (Burt L. Standish, 1901, Street & Smith; Gutenberg #62719)

Single book. No other books, except an ad-page at end for Merriwell Series No. 76 "Dick Merriwell at Fardale" (not part of story).

## Cast (key)
- Frank Merriwell: pitcher, Yale grad, "Merry"; double-shoot pitch (wrist sprained earlier; wrist worsens through book).
- Dick Merriwell: Frank's younger half-brother, ~14, pitches jump ball and drop; can throw with either hand; raised in West (Pleasant Valley, near Lake Sunshine, under Rockies); sweetheart Felicia (Little Star Eyes), daughter of Mr. Delores (Spanish refugee, Juan Delores).
- Old Joe Crowfoot: aged Indian, Dick's mentor, "Injun Heart" calls Dick; "Steady Hand" = Frank; smokes black pipe, dirty red blanket; speaks broken English ("Heap big," "Ugh!"); once tried to kill Frank; shot earlier, wounded.
- Bart Hodge: catcher; dark; sweetheart Elsie Bellwood.
- Inza Burrage: Yale girl, Frank's sweetheart; Elsie.
- Jack Ready: third-baseman, apple-cheeked, flowery speech ("Ye gods," "La! la!").
- Harry Rattleton: second-baseman, malapropisms ("dim-jandy," "spock the knots").
- Browning (Bruce): first-baseman, big, lazy.
- Carson (Berlin): short-stop/right-field.
- Greg Carker: socialist speeches, "earthquake."
- Gamp (Joe Gamp): long New Hampshire youth, center field, stutters.
- John Swiftwing: Indian, former Carlisle; left field.
- Merriwell team = "Merries."
- Hazen: stout red-faced gambler, stubby mustache; bets; tried to bribe Frank ($50→$100→$200, shoved money).
- Wescott: man in blue, friend of Hazen; bet $200 on Stars.
- Derring: crooked umpire (Jim Derring), bought by Hazen.
- Dorrity: captain/first-baseman of Omaha Stars; Batch: pitcher of Stars; Hanson: catcher/heavy hitter; Teller, Skew, O'Grady, Jack (second), Maloney, Corrigan, Carson-not; Wilson: Stars' manager.
- Chop Morrisy: replacement umpire.

## Book sequence
**Ch I–IV (Omaha, Stars game):** 7th inning; Frank's wrist twists; Dorrity protests; Frank walks two batters (two balls); Hanson hits ball; Gamp throws to plate, Bart tags Hanson at plate (out). Bases full; Corrigan's shot hits Ready; Ready throws ball down; Carker hit; Frank hits home run stretching 3-bagger; tie 2-2. Hazen tries to bribe Frank ($50 offer, $200 later); Frank flings money; Frank shakes Hazen. Derring signals Hazen; Derring makes calls against Merries (Gamp "strike" over head; Swiftwing catch dispute—umpire says he picked it up). Crowd mobs umpire; Frank protects Derring; Morrisy replaces Derring; Derring declares forfeit 9–0, rejected. Ninth: Maloney catch dispute (Teller dropped). Merries lose 2–3 on Gamp-related errors/Corrigan wild throws; Frank pitches with bad wrist, errors by support (Carson, Browning, Ready).

**Ch V–VI:** Team at hotel; Ready/Carker/Gamp talk; Frank challenges Stars (Wilson accepts, gate winner-take-all, day after tomorrow). Derring fights Frank outside hotel; Frank punches him, disarms Hazen's revolver (Hazen draws; Frank kicks it). Dick arrives in Omaha with Old Joe. Joe agrees to stay with Dick ("you be his father"). Dick bets Hazen $1,000 on game; Frank makes him donate winnings to charity. Dick: "Steady Hand" references.

**Ch VII–IX (Omaha rematch):** Dick plays short; Dick makes catches (Hanson, Jack), bunts (Hodge bunts for hit, Gamp bunts). Frank hit: Browning steals, double play. Score tied 1–1 after 4th; Dick pitches from 5th; Dick throws jump ball, strikes out Maloney; game 1–1 through 9th. Dick's winning run: Bart's ground hit, Dick scores in 9th, Merries win 2–1. Hazen loses bets.

**Ch X–XIII (Minneapolis/St. Paul; "jay pitcher"):** Foley (St. Paul pitcher) spiked by Prince (Minneapolis); Foley's hand hurt. Frank disguised as country "jay" in old clothes, carroty hair, derby hat; volunteers as pitcher; name "Bill"; Joe Stammering friend (Joe, stutters) on bleachers. Jay strikes out batters; Frank hits home run stretching hit into home run (tie). Jay reveals "double-shoot" sickness: "curves both ways." Dowling (gambler) bribes jay ($200), jay punches him; mob; Dick and Old Joe and eight Yale friends fight thugs; they sing "Here's to good old Merry." Jay hits winning 1-run home run in 9th for St. Paul. Frank unmasked by crowd; manager challenges Minneapolis team, game next day.

**Ch XIV–XVI (Minneapolis challenge game):** Dowling/Bates (opium fiend) drug Frank's vichy water via cross-eyed waiter Pete. Frank dizzy; Potter pitcher; Dick pitches with either hand, jump ball, strikes out first three. Old Joe war-dance and war-whoop. Frank pitches back, home run over right-field fence in 9th; Merries win.

**Ch XVII–XIX (Philadelphia):** Robinson (Athletics manager) and Wilder challenge; Frank accepts. Ready and Frank bet/gate winner-take-all. Frank declines drinking/smoking. Squinty Jim McCann (bully) and boys mock Old Joe; Dick fights Squinty, wins. Officer's boy inspired by Frank; officer shakes Frank's hand.

**Ch XX–XXV (Philadelphia Athletics game):** Bud McCann (brother of Squinty; prize-fighter, catcher) plots; Bud trips Frank with bat; Frank fights McCann. Dick hurt by McCann's knees in a slide (face bloody); Frank hits McCann repeatedly. Athletics lead 4–2. Old Joe brought by Greg; Joe's yell; Dick hits (Merries rally: Ready, Frank hits scoring, Dick triple play — Dick catches fly, runs to second, tags Webster, tags Robinson). Score 5–4 Merries.

**Ch XXVI–XXIX (New York; The Mysteries):** Jack Hazard (white-haired youth, 60-ish face) challenges Merries to Polo Grounds; team "The Mysteries" = Yale friends: Gene Skelding (reformed), Starbright, Mason, Oliver Packard, Dismal Jones, Hans Dunnerwurst, Barney Mulloy, Ephraim Gallup, Dade Morgan (pitcher). Frank sends Dick to pitch. Man with dog Nero bets Dick won't last 4 innings; Inza takes bet pool ($200 stakeholder Robert Harding). Dick homesick (Felicia, Pleasant Valley); Old Joe advises.

**Ch XXX–XXXIII (Polo Grounds game):** Dick pitches; gives up hits; Yale men cheer; Dick strikes out batters (Jones, Gene); Hodge fans batters. Dog Nero attacks Dick; Dick throws ball into dog's mouth; Old Joe kills the dog with knife. Dog's owner threatens; Frank intervenes; police search Joe—knife hidden (Berlin Carson took it). Morgan's team leads; Hodge scores; Dick and Frank tie; Dick stole home for winning run in 9th. Inza gives Dick the Yale blue badge; Elsie kisses Dick. Ends.

## Score/key facts
- Omaha: Stars 2, Merries 3 (lost 2–3 first game, Omaha game 2 Merries won 2–1).
- Frank stolen home/3-bagger tie; home run over fence in Minneapolis; triple play by Dick in Athletics game; Dick steals home wins final game. Final tallied.
- Frank's bad wrist: sprain earlier; Dick's jump ball new skill.
- Frank's sickness from drugged vichy (Ch XVII); Frank poisoned by Dowling/Pete.
- Quotes: "Heap good work," "Steady Hand," "Injun Heart," "Frank Merriwell's double-shoot," "Triple play," "Dick Merriwell at Fardale" No. 76 ad.
